newsitem.title: MEXICO: 9 phone firms to invest $5.8 bln in Mexico-Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: 9 phone firms to invest $5.8 bln in Mexico-Zedillo.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said Friday that nine telephone companies entering the Mexican market as of 1997 will invest $5.8 billion in the country over the next four years.

"Today we have nine companies that have just entered the market that have promised to invest nearly $5.8 billion, which means the creation of 17,000 new jobs, in the course of the next four years," Zedillo told a convention of telephone workers.

The new phone companies will be allowed to compete for domestic customers starting January 1, 1997, as Telefonos de Mexico loses its monopoly status. Some of the new competitors began serving corporate clients as of August.
Among the new companies doing business in Mexico is Alestra, an alliance among AT&T Corp, GTE Corp, Grupo Financiero Bancomer, Grupo Industrial Alfa SA de CV and Telefonica de Espana.
Another new competitor is Avantel, an alliance of MCI Communications Corp and Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival.
The federal telecommunications law that opened Mexico to competition "makes transparant the honoring of concessions, gives security to investment and promotes options for the consumer," Zedillo said.
